Name: PowerShell Encoded Command
Description: Uses -enc/-EncodedCommand to run a base64-encoded script, hiding its real content from casual inspection.

Name: Hidden Window Flag
Description: Runs with a hidden window so the victim never sees a console appear.

Name: CMD Invocation
Description: Invokes the Windows command interpreter. Weak signal alone - extremely common in legitimate use.

Name: CMD /c Chaining
Description: Uses cmd /c to chain a command, common in ClickFix payloads that wrap the real attack in an extra shell layer.

Name: curl Download
Description: Uses curl to fetch remote content.

Name: wget Download
Description: Uses wget to fetch remote content.

Name: Invoke-WebRequest / iwr
Description: Uses PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest (iwr alias) to fetch remote content.

Name: Piped to Invoke-Expression
Description: Pipes downloaded content directly into Invoke-Expression (iex), executing it without any inspection - the classic 'download cradle' pattern.

Name: bitsadmin Transfer
Description: Uses bitsadmin /transfer, a LOLBin download technique with little legitimate interactive use.

Name: certutil Download/Decode
Description: Uses certutil -urlcache or -decode, a well-known LOLBin technique to download or decode a payload.

Name: mshta Execution
Description: Invokes mshta.exe, a classic HTA/remote-script execution LOLBin used heavily in ClickFix campaigns.

Name: regsvr32 Squiblydoo
Description: Matches the 'Squiblydoo' technique: regsvr32 registering a remote scriptlet via scrobj.dll.

Name: wscript Execution
Description: Invokes wscript.exe, commonly abused to launch obfuscated JScript/VBScript payloads.

Name: cscript Execution
Description: Invokes cscript.exe, commonly abused to launch obfuscated JScript/VBScript payloads.

Name: Long Base64-Like Blob
Description: Contains a long base64-alphabet run, a hallmark of an encoded/obfuscated payload. Low weight alone since this is generic; the engine's entropy bonus typically sharpens this further.

Name: Excessive Symbol Chaining
Description: Contains an unusually dense run of shell metacharacters, typical of obfuscated one-liners.
